title_original: 【開幕】特別展「生きものたちの性」国立科学博物館で2027年2月21日まで　「いのち」をつなぐための戦略　多様な性の理由を知る
editorial_title_zh: 【开幕】特别展“生物的性”国立科学博物馆将展至2027年2月21日 连结“生命”的策略 了解多样性之“性”背后的原因
editorial_excerpt_zh: 国立科学博物馆（东京·上野公园）特别展“生物的性”将于10月31日开幕。展期将是一场持续至2027年2月21日的超长展览。这是国立科学博物馆首次以“性”为主题，迫近生物所拥有的多样性之性的姿态与

"雄性＞雌性并非多数派？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展厅开篇便陈列着对比雌雄的生物标本，十分吸引眼球。能轻易分辨的雌雄人们早已习以为常。在雄性体型较大的生物种类中，认为体型大在争夺雌性的过程中更有利，因此大型个体的基因得以保留。相反，雌性体型较大在孕育幼崽或卵时具有一定优势，据说在两栖类、鱼类、昆虫类、无脊椎动物等整体中反而是多数派。这据说是由于小型动物需要产下大量卵。令人意外的是，即使在哺乳类中，鲸类和蝙蝠类也是雌性更大。在雄性极端小型化的极端例子中，据说有鮟鱇鱼在附着于雌性身上的过程中，变得像是雌性器官的一部分这样的例子。", "heading", "text": "雌雄同体的动物", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "融合了雌雄特征的动物展示令人惊叹。展示的茶花鸡鸡冠很大，右脚具有雄性特征的距，但左脚和短短的尾羽则偏向雌性。昆虫方面则介绍了左右花纹不同的蛾、以及长着短头角独角仙等。据说这些被称为雌雄嵌合体（Gynandromorph）。请前往现场亲眼观看。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本以为由基因决定性别是常识，但实际上这只是哺乳类的特征，令人惊讶的是，许多生物是由其他因素（例如成长环境）来决定的。电影《海底总动员》中大家熟知的小丑鱼，全部作为雄性长大，但群落中体型最大的个体会变成雌性。相反，一种名为隆头鱼的鱼类在日本也能见到，在成长过程中虽然是雌性，但长大后额头会隆起并变成雄性。对于物种而言，体型大的个体变成雄性还是雌性更有利呢，这让人脑子有点乱。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/22235.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“性的决定”展示场景", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "赢得青睐的途径也各有不同", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有趣的是介绍雄性为了博取青睐而使出各种手段的展览。有一种栖息在西伯利亚的鸟类名为流苏鹬，说明中指出其雄性也分为3种类型。“领地型”属于硬汉派，外观也是华丽的花纹。“卫星型”则是攻击性较低、在领地型周围企图分一杯羹的类型。其白色外观仿佛要抹去自身存在一般。更绝的是所谓的“雌性拟态型”，据说这种雄性外观变得与雌性一模一样并靠近雌性。鼻子越大越受欢迎的是长鼻猴。这明显与受欢迎程度呈正相关，据说鼻子大的雄性能够拥有庞大的后宫。", "在吸引异性的策略中，像翠鸟那样雄性向雌性赠送食物的礼物战术（求爱喂食）非常独特。利用光线进行吸引的萤火虫闪烁战术也广为人知。雌蚕蛾释放出信息素吸引并让雄蛾起舞的舞蹈也十分引人入胜。在会场的大屏幕上，请仔细欣赏现代艺术家玛丽亚·费尔南达·卡多佐将澳大利亚孔雀蝇属的求爱行为融入声音与振动的影像作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "展厅内配备了丰富的影像显示屏。由于每一段都相对较短，且全都是捕捉到决定性瞬间的内容，因此很想逐一观看。此外，漫画解说也极其精彩。即便对解说一知半解，看了漫画也会拍案叫绝道：“原来如此，是这么回事啊。”通览下来，动物、植物性的多样性必定会让所有人大开眼界。如此不可思议的世界着实难得一见。（读卖新闻美术展导航编辑班·丸山谦一）", "translated": true}, {"type": "開幕セレモニーでは、総合監修を務めた一人の同館顧問の篠田謙一さんが「館長をしていたときに、『性のことをなぜ語れないのだろう』と思って、多様な生物全体の性の話をする展覧会を企画した」と狙いを明かしました。確かに、性差も求愛行動も生殖の仕組みもどれも面白そうなテーマです。続いて、公式アンバサダーとして、お笑いタレントの二人組ラランド（サーヤ、ニシダ）が登場しました。サーヤさんはNHKのEテレで「性」の諸問題を学問的に扱う「はなしちゃお！～性と生の学問～」のMCを務めているので、本展のPRには適役です。音声ガイドも務めましたが、二人は「もっと知ってもらいたいことがたくさんあった」とパッションを押さえきれない様子でした。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/KAON5336-scaled.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "公式アンバサダー、ラランドの二人　撮影・青山謙太郎", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "オス＞メスは多数派ではない？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会場には、序盤から雌雄を比較する生きものの標本が並んでいて引き寄せられました。簡単に違いの分かるオスメスは馴染みがあります。オスが大きい種類の生物は、メスを巡る争いに体の大きい方が有利なので、大型の個体の遺伝子が残ったと考えられています。逆にメスが大きい方が、子や卵を宿す上で有利な面があり、両生類や魚類、昆虫類、無脊椎動物など、全体ではむしろ多数派だそうです。小型動物は大量の卵を産む必要があるからだとか。哺乳類でもクジラ類やコウモリ類はメスの方が大きいとは意外でした。オスが小型化してしまった極端な例では、メスにくっついているうちにメスの臓器のようになってしまったアンコウ類の例があるそうです。"}, "text": "オスとメスの特徴が混ざってしまった動物の展示には驚きました。展示されたチャボは鶏冠が大きく右足にオスの特徴の蹴爪がありますが、左足と短い尾羽はメス的です。昆虫では左右の柄が違う蛾や、短い頭角のついたカブトムシなどが紹介されていました。これらはギナンドロモルフ（雌雄モザイク）と呼ぶそうです。現地でご覧ください。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "paragraph", "text": "性が遺伝子で決まるのは常識だと思っていましたが、実はそれは哺乳類の特徴であって、それ以外の要因、例えば成長する環境で決まる生物も多いというのは驚きました。映画「ファインディング・ニモ」でおなじみのカクレクマノミは、すべてオスとして育ちますが、群れの中で一番大きな個体がメスになるのだそうです。逆に、コブダイという日本にもいる魚は、成長するまではメスなのに、大きく育つとおでこにこぶが出てきてオスに変わるそうです。大きい個体はオスとメスのどちらになる方が種にとって有利なのか、頭が混乱してきました。"}, article_text:
国立科学博物館（東京・上野公園）で特別展「生きものたちの性」が10月31日に開幕を迎えます。会期は2027年2月21日までのロングラン。国立科学博物館として初めて“性”をテーマに据えた、生きものがもつ多様な性のすがたとその仕組みに迫る特別展です。開幕前日の内覧会を取材しました。

特別展「生きものたちの性」

会場：国立科学博物館（東京都台東区上野公園7-20）

会期：2026年10月31日（土）～2027年2月21日(日)

開館時間：9時～17時(入場は16時30分まで)

休館日：毎週月曜日、11月4日(水)、11月24日(火)、12月28日(月)～1月1日(金・祝)、1月12日(火) ※ただし、11月2日(月)、23日(月・祝)、1月11日(月・祝)、2月15日(月)は開館

入場料：一般・大学生2,300円（2,100円）、小・中・高校生600円（500円） ※（ ）は前売り料金

アクセス：JR「上野駅」公園口より徒歩5分／東京メトロ銀座線・日比谷線「上野駅」より徒歩10分

詳細は、 展覧会公式サイト または 国立科学博物館公式サイト まで。

「生物全体の性を語ろう」

開幕セレモニーでは、総合監修を務めた一人の同館顧問の篠田謙一さんが「館長をしていたときに、『性のことをなぜ語れないのだろう』と思って、多様な生物全体の性の話をする展覧会を企画した」と狙いを明かしました。確かに、性差も求愛行動も生殖の仕組みもどれも面白そうなテーマです。続いて、公式アンバサダーとして、お笑いタレントの二人組ラランド（サーヤ、ニシダ）が登場しました。サーヤさんはNHKのEテレで「性」の諸問題を学問的に扱う「はなしちゃお！～性と生の学問～」のMCを務めているので、本展のPRには適役です。音声ガイドも務めましたが、二人は「もっと知ってもらいたいことがたくさんあった」とパッションを押さえきれない様子でした。

オス＞メスは多数派ではない？

会場には、序盤から雌雄を比較する生きものの標本が並んでいて引き寄せられました。簡単に違いの分かるオスメスは馴染みがあります。オスが大きい種類の生物は、メスを巡る争いに体の大きい方が有利なので、大型の個体の遺伝子が残ったと考えられています。逆にメスが大きい方が、子や卵を宿す上で有利な面があり、両生類や魚類、昆虫類、無脊椎動物など、全体ではむしろ多数派だそうです。小型動物は大量の卵を産む必要があるからだとか。哺乳類でもクジラ類やコウモリ類はメスの方が大きいとは意外でした。オスが小型化してしまった極端な例では、メスにくっついているうちにメスの臓器のようになってしまったアンコウ類の例があるそうです。

雌雄が混ざった動物

オスとメスの特徴が混ざってしまった動物の展示には驚きました。展示されたチャボは鶏冠が大きく右足にオスの特徴の蹴爪がありますが、左足と短い尾羽はメス的です。昆虫では左右の柄が違う蛾や、短い頭角のついたカブトムシなどが紹介されていました。これらはギナンドロモルフ（雌雄モザイク）と呼ぶそうです。現地でご覧ください。

性の決定は遺伝子だけじゃない

性が遺伝子で決まるのは常識だと思っていましたが、実はそれは哺乳類の特徴であって、それ以外の要因、例えば成長する環境で決まる生物も多いというのは驚きました。映画「ファインディング・ニモ」でおなじみのカクレクマノミは、すべてオスとして育ちますが、群れの中で一番大きな個体がメスになるのだそうです。逆に、コブダイという日本にもいる魚は、成長するまではメスなのに、大きく育つとおでこにこぶが出てきてオスに変わるそうです。大きい個体はオスとメスのどちらになる方が種にとって有利なのか、頭が混乱してきました。

モテモテになる道にもいろいろ

面白かったのは、オスがモテるためのあの手この手を紹介した展示です。エリマキシギというシベリアの鳥は、オスにも3タイプいると説明されていました。「なわばり型」は剛腕タイプで見た目も派手な柄です。「サテライト型」は攻撃性が低くなわばり型の周りでおこぼれを狙うタイプ。存在を消すかのような白い色です。さらに「メス擬態型」というのが傑作で、見た目もメスそっくりになってメスに近づくオスだそうです。 鼻が大きいほどモテるのはテングザル。明らかにモテ度と相関関係があって、鼻の大きなオスは大きなハレムをもてるのだそうです。

鳴かぬ蛍が 身を焦がす

異性を惹きつける戦略では、カワセミのようにオスがメスに餌を贈るプレゼント作戦（求愛給餌）はユニークです。光でアピールする蛍の明滅作戦もよく知られています。メスのカイコガが出すフェロモンに引き寄せられて踊るオスのダンスも興味深いものでした。会場の大きなスクリーンでは、豪州のクジャクハエトリグモ属の求愛行動にサウンドと振動を加えた現代芸術家マリア・フェルナンダ・カルドーゾさんの映像作品をじっくりご覧ください。

バトルも避けられない

平和的にカップルが誕生しなければ、闘争で配偶者を得る場面が待っています。メスにしても、強く優良なオスの遺伝子を残すために勝者を迎え入れるそうです。弱肉強食は厳しい。腕っぷし以外に生きる道があって、人間で良かった。

会場には、豊富な映像のディスプレイが備えられています。それぞれが割と短編で、決定的瞬間を捉えているものばかりなので、一つひとつ見ていきたいものです。また、漫画解説が秀逸です。解説が飲み込めなくても、漫画を見ると「なるほど、そういうことか」と膝を打つことでしょう。通してみると、動物、植物の性の多様性には、誰もが目を見開かされるはずです。こんなに不思議な世界はなかなか見られません。（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班・丸山謙一）

※本展では「生きものの性」をテーマとしており、性的な表現が含まれます。ご来場の際は、内容をご理解のうえご判断ください。すべての生きものに恋愛感情が認められているわけではありませんが、本展では一般に理解しやすい表現として「恋」「愛」という言葉を用いています。画像はイメージです。画像の生物は標本または映像で紹介します。

article_text:
Bassist for Hole and later the Smashing Pumpkins, the Montreal-born musician brings more than two hundred photographs from the heart of the grunge years to Toronto. An intimate, searing archive of the last analogue decade.

By Guénola Pellen. Photos by Melissa Auf der Maur .

When she joined Hole in the summer of 1994, the bassist and photographer Melissa Auf der Maur had one unusual clause written into her contract. A roll of 35mm film was to be waiting for her backstage at every show. Billy Corgan, of the Smashing Pumpkins, had recommended her to Courtney Love. Their album Live Through This had hit stores four days after Kurt Cobain, Love’s husband and Nirvana’s founder, was found dead. Kristen Pfaff, whose place on bass she took, had died of an overdose. She was stepping into a band in mourning.

Born in Montreal in 1972, she had been taking photographs since the age of thirteen, and found behind the lens, and in the darkroom, a shelter for her shyness. At Concordia University, in her home city, her professor Raymonde April, a celebrated Quebec photographer, introduced her to Francesca Woodman, the American who made herself her own subject, her body dissolved by the long exposure, in rooms left to ruin.

Melissa Auf der Maur turned Hole down at first, meaning to begin a master’s in photography. Then she changed her mind. “I remember being on Canal Street and asking for the most durable point-and-shoot Nikon,” she told The New Yorker. “I knew I was on assignment.” Press photographers are allowed the first three songs from the pit and nothing more. Nobody was timing her. With a self-timer and a cable release, she caught herself mid-song. With the Smashing Pumpkins, she would go on to mount the camera on her amplifier.

The photographs in “My ’90s Rock Photographs” breathe the camaraderie of the road. The band poses at a dressing-room mirror, above a catering table strewn with paper cups and coffee pots. The flash bursts in the glass, and Courtney Love, in an ivory slip, stares the lens down. Elsewhere she pedals barefoot on a bicycle down an empty concrete corridor. Against the barriers, teenage girls with damp hair press together, all smiles. Thirty years have passed. And with them, a whole generation is looking back over Melissa Auf der Maur’s shoulder. generation is looking back over her shoulder.

“My ’90s Rock Photographs” runs through June 6, 2027, at the Art Gallery of Ontario , Toronto.

The book My ’90s Rock Photographs is published by DelMonico Books , 240 pages, $49.95.

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "UJ 美术馆馆长迪内克·奥尔顿（Dineke Orton）博士表示：“热烈祝贺所有参加今年 MTN x UJ 新当代艺术奖的艺术家，并特别向我们实至名归的2026年得主西姆尼基韦致以敬意。这一殊荣是她当之无愧的，我们热切期待看到她继续以其展览作品所展现的那种无畏精神和创作信念，在已经十分引人注目的职业生涯上再创辉煌。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "出生于约翰内斯堡、常驻阿姆斯特丹的布胡隆古，其以研究为主导的实践探讨了知识是如何产生的、由谁产生以及如何流通。她的创作横跨声音、文本、装置和出版领域，通过层层交织的聆听与感知生态，探究社会历史及日常生活现象。她的工作经常通过留出疏漏、疑问以及不可言说之余地的方法人手，探讨（非）物质的存在与年表问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她为 MTN x UJ 新当代艺术奖呈献的迭代声音装置根植于福音音乐与侨民记忆，探讨了黑人流动性与集体聆听的历史。西瑟尔将该作品形容为“一进入便极具冲击力”，并补充道：“它明确地为层层交织的互动保留了空间。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "穆什瓦纳补充道：“西姆尼基韦以一种游走在可及性边缘的方式提炼观念，同时邀请观众从多种视角参与聆听、攀爬和观看的行为。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artthrob.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/unnamed-240x300.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtThrob", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "西姆尼基韦·布胡隆古（Simnikiwe Buhlungu），亮相于2026年展览《Holding sp(l)ace for the in__between》。马坎达", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在接受该奖项时，布胡隆古致辞道：“向 UJ、MTN 基金会、国家艺术节和伊齐科各团队致以无限、循环、丰沛的感激。致塞科托（Sekoto）及其现象学创意后代。致朋友和家人。致负责混音和母带制作的 PrichA。致声音、空间、时间以及那不可察觉的事物。致知识。致实践。”自2025年以来，马莱杜引导艺术家们达到了深度与自信的新高度，呈现出一个充满青春活力、创造力与创新精神的展览。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "奥尔顿表示：“我们有幸与担任 MTN x UJ 新当代艺术策展人的马莱杜合作，她以非凡的视野和关怀将这些卓越的艺术之声汇聚在一起。马莱杜确保了每位艺术家独特的视角和意图不仅得以保留，而且以一种醒目、连贯的方式呈现。这场展览证明了马莱杜的策展敏感性，以及她创造一个让多元实践进行有意义对话的的空间的能力。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为国家艺术节的一部分，将持续至2026年7月5日的《Holding sp(l)ace for the in__between》立足于当下时刻的复杂性之中，拒绝了主题展览的常规框架，而是将当代性作为展览的一种特征。它通过声音、土地、家园和呼吸，探讨了拒绝、集体生存和黑人女性主义思想等问题。该展览体现了对批判性艺术实践和具有社会参与性的文化对话的承诺。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "奥尔顿表示：“感谢 NCA 艺术家、策展人，以及国家艺术节上让这一届活动取得巨大成功的卓越团队——感谢你们让我们想起合作、创造力和创新所具有的变革力量。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "奥尔顿总结道：“我们来自 MTN 南非基金会的长期合作伙伴和家人，再次展现了他们对这一合作伙伴关系及 NCA 项目坚定不移的承诺。我们同样庆幸并极其感激我们的其他执行合作伙伴：马坎达国家艺术节尊贵的管理团队，以及位于开普敦的南非伊齐科博物馆，感谢他们让我们有机会在整个2026年展出并分享这一项目与合作。没有你们的奉献、支持和关注，我们绝无可能实现这一切，我们感谢你们给予的这个非凡机会，得以延续 MTN x UJ 新当代艺术奖项目的传奇与影响力。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "quote", "text": "展览场地：国家艺术节纪念大楼（The Monument Building）环形画廊（Gallery in the Round）与新画廊（New Gallery），马坎达\n展期：2026年6月26日 – 7月5日", "translated": true}]

article_text:
A news item by ArtThrob Editors on the 30th of June 2026. This should take you 3 minutes to read.

National Arts Festival 25.06 - 05.07.2026

On 26 June 2026, Simnikiwe Buhlungu was announced as the winner of the MTN x UJ New Contemporaries Award at the opening ceremony held at the Monument Building during the National Arts Festival in Makhanda.

Presented by UJ Art Gallery, in partnership with the MTN SA Foundation and with institutional support from Iziko Museums South Africa, the MTN x UJ New Contemporaries Award (NCA) exhibition – Holding sp(l)ace for the in__between – is curated by Amogelang Maledu and includes the work of Buhlungu, Zara Julius, thato makatu, and Unathi Mkonto.

The winner of the MTN x UJ New Contemporaries Award was selected by an independent panel of adjudicators, including Christine Dixie, Shalom Mushwana and Rucera Seethal. As the winner, Buhlungu receives a R100 000 cash prize.

“A huge congratulations to all the artists who participated in this year’s MTN x UJ New Contemporaries Award, and a special acknowledgement to our deserving winner for 2026, Simnikiwe. This recognition is thoroughly well earned, and we eagerly anticipate watching her continue to build on an already compelling career with the same fearlessness and creative conviction that distinguishes her work in this exhibition,” says Dr Dineke Orton, UJ Art Gallery Curator.

Johannesburg-born, Amsterdam-based Buhlungu’s research-led practice explores how knowledge is produced, by whom, and how it circulates. She works across sound, text, installation, and publishing, investigating socio-historical and everyday phenomena through layered ecologies of listening and sensing. Her work often engages questions of (im)material presences and chronologies through methodologies that leave gaps for slippages, questions and that which is not articulable.

Her iterative sound installation presented at the MTN x UJ New Contemporaries Award is rooted in gospel and diasporic memory and engages histories of Black mobility and collective listening. Seethal describes the work as “impactful on entering”, adding that “it holds space definitively for layered engagement.”

“Simnikiwe distils ideas in ways that exist on the edge of accessibility, whilst inviting the viewer to participate in the act of listening, climbing and viewing from a variety of perspectives,” adds Mushwana.

Simnikiwe Buhlungu, presenting in the exhibition ‘Holding sp(l)ace for the in__between’, 2026. Makhanda

In her acceptance of the award, Buhlungu offered “An infinite, cyclical, abounding overwhelm of gratitude to the teams at UJ, MTN Foundation, National Arts Festival and Iziko. To Sekoto and his phenomenological creative progenies. To friends and family. To PrichA for mixing and mastering. To sound, space, time, and that which is imperceptible. To knowledges. To practice.” Since 2025, Maledu has guided the artists to new levels of depth and confidence, resulting in an exhibition that pulses with youthfulness, creativity, and innovation.”

We have been immensely privileged to work with Maledu as the MTN x UJ New Contemporaries Curator, who brought together these remarkable artistic voices with exceptional vision and care. Maledu ensured that each artist’s unique perspective and intention was not only preserved but presented in a striking, cohesive manner. The exhibition stands as a testament to Maledu’s curatorial sensitivity and ability to create a space where diverse practices can converse meaningfully,” says Orton.

‘Holding sp(l)ace for the in__between’, which runs until 5 July 2026 as part of the National Arts Festival, is situated within the complexities of the contemporary moment, refusing the general framework of themed exhibitions and instead makes contemporaneity a character of the exhibition. It engages questions of refusal, collective survival, and Black feminist thought through sound, land, home, and breath. The exhibition reflects a commitment to critical artistic practice and socially engaged cultural dialogue.

“To the NCA artists, the curator, and the incredible team at the National Arts Festival who made this edition such a resounding success – thank you for reminding us of the transformative power of collaboration, creativity, and innovation,” says Orton.

“Our longstanding partners, and family, from the MTN SA Foundation have once again demonstrated their unwavering commitment to the partnership and the NCA programme. We are also privileged and immensely grateful to our additional implementing partners; the esteemed management team for the National Arts Festival in Makhanda, and the Iziko Museums South Africa in Cape Town, for allowing us the opportunity to feature and share this project and partnership throughout 2026. We truly could not have accomplished this without your dedication, support, and interest, and we thank you for this astonishing opportunity to continue the legacy and impact of the MTN x UJ New Contemporaries Award programme,” concluded Orton.

Exhibition Venue: Gallery in the Round and New Gallery, The Monument Building, National Arts Festival, Makhanda Dates: 26 June – 5 July 2026

title_original: 【磯田道史の歴史をゆく】「秀吉と幻の首都・伏見」　10月21日放送　BS日テレ　世界的な観光地、かつては政治の中心だった
editorial_title_zh: 【磯田道史的历史之旅】「秀吉与幻之首都·伏见」 10月21日播出 BS日テレ 世界著名旅游地，曾是政治中心
editorial_excerpt_zh: 磯田先生独特的视角和精妙的叙述方式。通过通俗易懂的解说，揭开历史的『真相』与『浪漫』的历史同行采访节目。《磯田道史的历史之旅》 ◇秀吉与幻之首都·伏见◇ 播出时间：2026年10月21日（周三）晚上9点～
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/638e55a953d6e5b3bd65628e3a0f6310.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "磯田先生独特的视角和精妙的叙述方式。通过通俗易懂的解说，揭开历史的『真相』与『浪漫』的历史同行采访节目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本次节目以如今成为世界著名旅游地的京都·伏见为舞台，围绕「秀吉与幻之首都·伏见」展开调查，包括以千本鸟居闻名的「伏见稻荷大社」等地点。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然丰臣秀吉给人的印象是大阪，但其实他晚年隐居的城和政治据点是「伏见城」。秀吉去世后，伏见城被德川家康继承，德川秀忠、家光也在此接受将军宣下，江户幕府的基础可以说是「Made in Fushimi」！？ 本次节目将从现存的“幻之伏见城”的痕迹（如小学校内残留的巨大石垣和神社的金箔瓦）出发，揭示大名屋敷起源的奇特町名，以及伏见酒（日本酒）发展中隐藏的城市规划之谜，解开天下人不为人知的历史浪漫。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/be689d4a7bc8e366fd6b01586f622bc2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/c3ca57450fac18141989df23f4e2f3d2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "■ 节目看点 ① 小学内至今仍沉睡的「可前往参观的伏见城」巨大石垣 以伏见历史研究第一人若林正博氏为「伏见的师傅」，潜入当地小学。调查昭和52年发现的伏见城石垣时，从用于凿石的「矢穴（yaana）」形状，浮现出初期筑城（秀吉·家康时代）的特征。此外，还揭示了「安土桃山时代」的「桃山」名称背后隐藏的，废城后悲伤的遗迹利用历史？ ② 豪华绚烂！「金箔瓦」与关原前哨战的真实发掘物 在御香宫神社保存的出土品调查中，不仅城内，就连大名屋敷的屋顶也被装饰的豪华绚烂的「金箔瓦」整齐排列。此外，还发现了在关原之战前哨战「伏见城之战」中烧毁的痕迹的瓦片，以及笼城兵无法食用的「烤成圆形的饭团」！历史的真实证据让磯田先生兴奋不已。 ③ 伊达政宗·石田三成·岛津…刻在町名上的战国武将们的名字 伏见的街道中至今仍保留着「桃山町正宗」「治部正丸」等战国武将的屋敷遗迹作为町名。通过比较现代地图与古地图，证明伏见街道中残留的「武家首都」的规模感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "（美术展导航编辑部）", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/638e55a953d6e5b3bd65628e3a0f6310.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "磯田先生のユニークな視点と絶妙な語り口。わかりやすい解説で歴史の『真実』と『ロマン』を解き明かす歴史同行取材番組です。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今回は、千本鳥居で知られる「伏見稲荷大社」をはじめ、今や世界的な観光地となった京都・伏見を舞台に「秀吉と幻の首都・伏見」と題して調査を敢行します。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大阪のイメージが強い豊臣秀吉ですが、実は最晩年に隠居城・政治の拠点として築いたのが「伏見城」でした。秀吉の死後、徳川家康へ受け継がれ、徳川秀忠・家光も将軍宣下を受けるなど、江戸幕府の基礎は「メイド・イン・伏見」だった！？ 今回は、現存しない“幻の伏見城”の痕跡（小学校に残る巨大石垣や神社の金箔瓦）から、大名屋敷がルーツとなった現在の珍しい町名、そして伏見酒（日本酒）の発展に隠された都市計画の謎まで、天下人たちの知られざる歴史ロマンを紐解きます。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/be689d4a7bc8e366fd6b01586f622bc2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/c3ca57450fac18141989df23f4e2f3d2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "■ 番組の見どころ ①小学校に現代も眠る「会いに行ける伏見城」の巨大石垣 伏見の歴史研究第一人者・若林正博氏を「伏見の師匠」として迎え、地元の小学校へ潜入。昭和52年に発見された伏見城の石垣を調査すると、石を割るための「矢穴（やあな）」の形状から、初期築城（秀吉・家康時代）の特徴が浮かび上がります。さらに「安土桃山時代」の“桃山”の由来に隠された、廃城後の切ない跡地利用の歴史とは？ ②豪華絢爛！「金箔瓦」と関ヶ原前哨戦のリアルな発掘物 御香宮神社に保管されている出土品調査では、城内だけでなく大名屋敷の屋根をも彩った豪華絢爛な「金箔瓦」がずらり。さらに、関ヶ原の戦いの前哨戦「伏見城の戦い」で焼け落ちた痕跡を残す瓦や、籠城兵が食べられなかった「丸焼きおにぎり」まで発見！歴史のリアルな証拠に磯田先生も大興奮。 ③伊達政宗・石田三成・島津…町名に刻まれた戦国武将たちの名残 「桃山町正宗」「治部正丸」など、伏見の街には今も戦国武将の屋敷跡がそのまま町名として残されています。現代の地図と古地図を比較しながら、伏見の街並みに残る「武家首都」のスケール感を実証します。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "（美術展ナビ編集班）"}]
article_text:
磯田先生のユニークな視点と絶妙な語り口。わかりやすい解説で歴史の『真実』と『ロマン』を解き明かす歴史同行取材番組です。

今回は、千本鳥居で知られる「伏見稲荷大社」をはじめ、今や世界的な観光地となった京都・伏見を舞台に「秀吉と幻の首都・伏見」と題して調査を敢行します。

大阪のイメージが強い豊臣秀吉ですが、実は最晩年に隠居城・政治の拠点として築いたのが「伏見城」でした。秀吉の死後、徳川家康へ受け継がれ、徳川秀忠・家光も将軍宣下を受けるなど、江戸幕府の基礎は「メイド・イン・伏見」だった！？ 今回は、現存しない“幻の伏見城”の痕跡（小学校に残る巨大石垣や神社の金箔瓦）から、大名屋敷がルーツとなった現在の珍しい町名、そして伏見酒（日本酒）の発展に隠された都市計画の謎まで、天下人たちの知られざる歴史ロマンを紐解きます。

■ 番組の見どころ ①小学校に現代も眠る「会いに行ける伏見城」の巨大石垣 伏見の歴史研究第一人者・若林正博氏を「伏見の師匠」として迎え、地元の小学校へ潜入。昭和52年に発見された伏見城の石垣を調査すると、石を割るための「矢穴（やあな）」の形状から、初期築城（秀吉・家康時代）の特徴が浮かび上がります。さらに「安土桃山時代」の“桃山”の由来に隠された、廃城後の切ない跡地利用の歴史とは？ ②豪華絢爛！「金箔瓦」と関ヶ原前哨戦のリアルな発掘物 御香宮神社に保管されている出土品調査では、城内だけでなく大名屋敷の屋根をも彩った豪華絢爛な「金箔瓦」がずらり。さらに、関ヶ原の戦いの前哨戦「伏見城の戦い」で焼け落ちた痕跡を残す瓦や、籠城兵が食べられなかった「丸焼きおにぎり」まで発見！歴史のリアルな証拠に磯田先生も大興奮。 ③伊達政宗・石田三成・島津…町名に刻まれた戦国武将たちの名残 「桃山町正宗」「治部正丸」など、伏見の街には今も戦国武将の屋敷跡がそのまま町名として残されています。現代の地図と古地図を比較しながら、伏見の街並みに残る「武家首都」のスケール感を実証します。

（美術展ナビ編集班）
article_author: アート・エキシビション・ジャパン

article_text:
Fang Zhaoling, Hon Chi-fun, Kan Tai-keung, Koo Mei, Kum Chi-keung, Eddie Lui, Lui Shou-kwan, Man Fung-yi, Mok Yat-san, Wucius Wong / Time Voyager / Nov 18, 2026 – Jan 30, 2027 / Opening: Wednesday, Nov 18, 5.30pm – 7.30pm /

Alisan Fine Arts 21/F Lyndhurst Tower 1 Lyndhurst Terrace, Central Hong Kong +852 2526 1091 Monday – Saturday, 10am – 6pm

alisan.com .hk

As Alisan Fine Arts unveils the final presentation of its 45th-anniversary programme, Then and Now , the gallery is pleased to present Time Voyager , a curatorial meditation on the evolution of Hong Kong art, told through the lens of the gallery itself. Ten artists, one city, four decades of change: the exhibition brings together distinguished contemporary Hong Kong artists whose relationship with Alisan Fine Arts reaches back to its founding in 1981. Brought into dialogue, their works trace the transformation of the city’s artistic landscape, offering a perspective that illuminates the present moment while resisting the fleeting currents of fashion.

Time Voyager is, in this sense, not so much a looking back as a return, but a homecoming to the rooms where these practices first took root. The ten artists assembled here are not strangers to the gallery; their histories have grown alongside its own, from the inaugural presentation at Société Générale in The Landmark, Central, and the early presentations devoted to Hong Kong art in 1983 and 1984, among them Contemporary Vision of 3 Hong Kong Artists , featuring Hon Chi-fun, and a solo exhibition for Lui Shou-kwan, pioneer of the New Ink Movement, to the landmark Lui Shou-kwan & His School at the Hong Kong Arts Centre in 1995, and onward through the embrace of ink installation and sculpture in the new millennium. To walk through the exhibition is to retrace a shared history, one in which Alice King’s early instinct for the quiet conversations between tradition and the contemporary has proven remarkably prescient. The works on view carry that inheritance forward, each bearing the trace of a relationship measured not in seasons but in decades.

This final chapter of Then and Now thus completes a larger whole. Where Now , opening at Alisan Atelier in December, gathers a younger generation whose conceptual inquiries mark a departure from academic tradition. Time Voyager returns to the artists who first defined the gallery’s voice, and who continue to renew it. Together, the two presentations bear witness to a consequential shift in Hong Kong’s art history, from the ink-rooted sensibilities of the 20th century to the expanded terrain of the present. The gallery now frames this passage through the very artists who journeyed through it: for forty-five years, Alisan Fine Arts has not simply documented the evolution of Hong Kong art but has helped to write the city’s unfolding story.

title_original: À Paris Photo, les visions fantastiques de Summer Wagner
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "La photographe et réalisatrice américaine Summer Wagner nous emmène dans son univers qui fait la part belle à l’imaginaire. Ses œuvres sont à retrouver sur les pages de Fisheye #79 , mais également sur les cimaises de Paris Photo du 12 au 15 novembre 2026.", "links": [{"text": "Fisheye #79", "url": "https://fisheyemagazine.fr/magazine/fisheye-79-quallons-nous-voir/"}, {"text": "Paris Photo", "url": "https://fisheyemagazine.fr/article/programmation-paris-photo-2026/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "On ignore si Summer Wagner, à la manière de David Lynch , se considère comme une scientifique de la condition humaine. On ignore donc ce qui est essentiel pour elle : fournir une vérité ou faire résonner une idée, transmettre une émotion ? Ce que l’on sait, c’est que la photographe et réalisatrice américaine aime ce qui reste en suspens, ce qui laisse place à l’imagination, faisant éclore des images pensées comme des métaphores, à même d’aller au-delà de ce qui est perceptible. Provoquer l’inédit, refuser d’avoir le final cut , telle semble être l’ambition de Summer Wagner, dont les différentes séries photographiques se traversent comme des rêves éveillés. Tout est là. Les hommes, les femmes, la romance, la fête, la jeunesse, son rapport aux réseaux sociaux, la ville, sa végétation, ses recoins les plus inexplorés. Pourtant, rien ne paraît totalement réel. Est-ce un fantasme ? Un souvenir ? Le mystère demeure, et c’est précisément cette incertitude qui rend la vision de ces images si stimulante.", "links": [{"text": "David Lynch", "url": "https://fisheyemagazine.fr/article/influence-david-lynch-photographie-emergente/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://fisheyeimmersive.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/the-invitation-1024x683.gif", "alt": "", "caption": "The invitation © Summer Wagner", "credit": "Fisheye"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Explorer l’inconscient"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Pour comprendre cet intérêt pour les scènes intemporelles, d’une étrange douceur, le mieux est encore de remonter le temps, jusqu’à l’enfance. C’est là, dit-elle, au sein d’une cabane perchée dans un arbre ou au bord d’un ruisseau en été, qu’elle écume les jours, seule, en imaginant tout un tas de scénarios aussi oniriques que profondément hantés par ses angoisses, ses doutes et tous ces sentiments qui la submergent au quotidien. « Je rejoue des tensions, des pertes, des moments d’ennui et des insécurités à travers des scènes dans lesquelles j’incarne une version passée de moi-même , confie-t-elle au blog About Photography. Je prends conscience que le fantôme d’une petite fille vit toujours en moi, et qu’il lui arrive encore de refaire surface. » En 2020, tout change. Après plusieurs années à réaliser des autoportraits, et après avoir étudié la production cinématographique à l’université, Summer Wagner profite de la pandémie pour emprunter l’appareil photo d’un ami et décide de se laisser porter par ses visions, son univers intérieur, qu’elle matérialise dans des clichés redevables à la grammaire du 7e art. Quoi de plus normal, après tout, quand on cite Andreï Tarkovski, Kristoffer Borgli et Yórgos Lánthimos en tant qu’influences principales, avant même de mentionner ne serait-ce qu’un photographe, en l’occurrence Gregory Crewdson, dont les images sont, elles aussi, fortement inspirées du cinéma. Désormais, il s’agit d’embrasser chacune de ses idées, de donner vie aux images qui l’obsèdent et, par conséquent, de définir une technique pour y parvenir. Celle-ci, à l’entendre, repose sur un procédé relativement simple, qu’elle résume ainsi : de longues expositions et un étalonnage des couleurs sur Adobe Lightroom."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://fisheyeimmersive.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/fe79-couv-abo-1-231x300.jpg", "alt": "couverture Fisheye Magazine #79", "caption": "", "credit": "Fisheye"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://fisheyeimmersive.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/wave-of-grass-777x1024.gif", "alt": "", "caption": "© Wave of grass Summer Wagner", "credit": "Fisheye"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://fisheyeimmersive.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ivy-street-1024x676.gif", "alt": "", "caption": "© Ivy Street Summer Wagner", "credit": "Fisheye"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Hors du temps"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Au fond, la singularité du travail de Summer Wagner se joue ailleurs, essentiellement dans son esprit. Celui d’une artiste qui ne semble obéir qu’à ses visions, de préférence les plus fantastiques. Midamerican Fever Dream , Pulse of Grass and Screen , The Parody of a Tangled Thread : toutes ses séries cultivent ainsi une forme d’ambiguïté. Certes, il y a de la tristesse, de la mélancolie et un certain nombre de personnes isolées dans les photographies de Summer Wagner. Certes, il semble impossible de ne pas songer aux peintures de Salman Toor ou Aaron Wiesenfeld qui mettent également en scène la solitude contemporaine. Mais cette lumière bleue, omniprésente, ce contraste des couleurs, cette atmosphère presque évanescente, cet espace accordé à la mémoire et aux réflexions introspectives qu’elle charrie, on ne peut pas faire comme si cela ne comptait pas. À Paris Photo, où elle présente six tirages au sein du secteur « Digital », c’est d’ailleurs ce sens de la nuance qui attire le regard, le trouble, le séduit. On comprend alors que Summer Wagner, aussi spirituelle soit-elle, ne se contente pas de créer des atmosphères. Ce qu’elle fige, c’est une vision écologique et animiste du monde, une réalité fantasmée, comme flottante et hors du temps, où le moindre élément (technologique, naturel, matériel) aspire au sublime. « Overgrowth at the Abandoned Millwood Plant » , dit l’une de ses œuvres. article_text:
La photographe et réalisatrice américaine Summer Wagner nous emmène dans son univers qui fait la part belle à l’imaginaire. Ses œuvres sont à retrouver sur les pages de Fisheye #79 , mais également sur les cimaises de Paris Photo du 12 au 15 novembre 2026.

On ignore si Summer Wagner, à la manière de David Lynch , se considère comme une scientifique de la condition humaine. On ignore donc ce qui est essentiel pour elle : fournir une vérité ou faire résonner une idée, transmettre une émotion ? Ce que l’on sait, c’est que la photographe et réalisatrice américaine aime ce qui reste en suspens, ce qui laisse place à l’imagination, faisant éclore des images pensées comme des métaphores, à même d’aller au-delà de ce qui est perceptible. Provoquer l’inédit, refuser d’avoir le final cut , telle semble être l’ambition de Summer Wagner, dont les différentes séries photographiques se traversent comme des rêves éveillés. Tout est là. Les hommes, les femmes, la romance, la fête, la jeunesse, son rapport aux réseaux sociaux, la ville, sa végétation, ses recoins les plus inexplorés. Pourtant, rien ne paraît totalement réel. Est-ce un fantasme ? Un souvenir ? Le mystère demeure, et c’est précisément cette incertitude qui rend la vision de ces images si stimulante.

Explorer l’inconscient

Pour comprendre cet intérêt pour les scènes intemporelles, d’une étrange douceur, le mieux est encore de remonter le temps, jusqu’à l’enfance. C’est là, dit-elle, au sein d’une cabane perchée dans un arbre ou au bord d’un ruisseau en été, qu’elle écume les jours, seule, en imaginant tout un tas de scénarios aussi oniriques que profondément hantés par ses angoisses, ses doutes et tous ces sentiments qui la submergent au quotidien. « Je rejoue des tensions, des pertes, des moments d’ennui et des insécurités à travers des scènes dans lesquelles j’incarne une version passée de moi-même , confie-t-elle au blog About Photography. Je prends conscience que le fantôme d’une petite fille vit toujours en moi, et qu’il lui arrive encore de refaire surface. » En 2020, tout change. Après plusieurs années à réaliser des autoportraits, et après avoir étudié la production cinématographique à l’université, Summer Wagner profite de la pandémie pour emprunter l’appareil photo d’un ami et décide de se laisser porter par ses visions, son univers intérieur, qu’elle matérialise dans des clichés redevables à la grammaire du 7e art. Quoi de plus normal, après tout, quand on cite Andreï Tarkovski, Kristoffer Borgli et Yórgos Lánthimos en tant qu’influences principales, avant même de mentionner ne serait-ce qu’un photographe, en l’occurrence Gregory Crewdson, dont les images sont, elles aussi, fortement inspirées du cinéma. Désormais, il s’agit d’embrasser chacune de ses idées, de donner vie aux images qui l’obsèdent et, par conséquent, de définir une technique pour y parvenir. Celle-ci, à l’entendre, repose sur un procédé relativement simple, qu’elle résume ainsi : de longues expositions et un étalonnage des couleurs sur Adobe Lightroom.

Hors du temps

Au fond, la singularité du travail de Summer Wagner se joue ailleurs, essentiellement dans son esprit. Celui d’une artiste qui ne semble obéir qu’à ses visions, de préférence les plus fantastiques. Midamerican Fever Dream , Pulse of Grass and Screen , The Parody of a Tangled Thread : toutes ses séries cultivent ainsi une forme d’ambiguïté. Certes, il y a de la tristesse, de la mélancolie et un certain nombre de personnes isolées dans les photographies de Summer Wagner. Certes, il semble impossible de ne pas songer aux peintures de Salman Toor ou Aaron Wiesenfeld qui mettent également en scène la solitude contemporaine. Mais cette lumière bleue, omniprésente, ce contraste des couleurs, cette atmosphère presque évanescente, cet espace accordé à la mémoire et aux réflexions introspectives qu’elle charrie, on ne peut pas faire comme si cela ne comptait pas. À Paris Photo, où elle présente six tirages au sein du secteur « Digital », c’est d’ailleurs ce sens de la nuance qui attire le regard, le trouble, le séduit. On comprend alors que Summer Wagner, aussi spirituelle soit-elle, ne se contente pas de créer des atmosphères. Ce qu’elle fige, c’est une vision écologique et animiste du monde, une réalité fantasmée, comme flottante et hors du temps, où le moindre élément (technologique, naturel, matériel) aspire au sublime. « Overgrowth at the Abandoned Millwood Plant » , dit l’une de ses œuvres. Son travail, c’est tout à fait ça : l’exploration d’un univers où les machines du capitalisme industriel semblent obsolètes, où seuls subsistent l’être humain, la végétation et la poésie qui peut surgir d’une telle rencontre lorsqu’elle est débarrassée du chaos extérieur, lorsqu’il ne flotte plus dans l’air qu’un parfum d’éternité.

Cet article est à retrouver dans Fisheye #79 .

article_text:
In America, fortune is often written in the plural of houses. Will Vogt owns three, which have also served as his hunting grounds as a photographer: a home in Corpus Christi, on the Texas Gulf coast; the family ranch, also in Texas; and, in Watch Hill, Rhode Island, the summer house where his family has gathered — and let themselves be photographed — for generations.

The boy he once was grew up elsewhere, in Haverford, Pennsylvania. More drawn to books than to sport, he discovered F. Scott Fitzgerald at boarding school, fell for his hero, Gatsby, and received his first camera not long after. From then on, it was his own world he turned the lens toward.

More than 70,000 images later, Will Vogt is far more than a chronicler of American wealth. His debut, These Americans , published in 2023, sold out. Three years later, Behind the Hedges returns to the same rituals — epic hunts, grand weddings, private society rallies — but the snapshot has given way to something more composed, and the urgency of youth to something more restrained. Interview.

Your previous book, These Americans , caught the moment. Behind the Hedges , your new book, composes it into tableaux. In practical terms, what changed in the way you shoot and sequence images between the two books?

Will Vogt: I’m not sure that the way I shoot changed as much as my material has. The advent of digital photography has also allowed me to capture more detail, which in turn makes larger tableau images possible.

These Americans drew heavily from photographs I took in the 1980s when I was younger and life around me was moving pretty fast. Behind the Hedges returns to many of the same people, places and traditions thirty years later. I’m older as are many of my subjects and as a result the pictures have slowed down a little too.

What did change enormously was my understanding of editing and sequencing. Before working with Jennifer Garza-Cuen on These Americans , I really had no idea how a photography book was put together. I learned that it isn’t a collection of your best photographs. In a book, the individual images have to work together, create a rhythm and tell a story.

In Behind the Hedges , your frame often leans on the natural or built architecture of a setting: a leading line draws the eye toward the façade of Lainston House, table and chairs arranged in the foreground; elsewhere, a swimming pool fills the foreground of the image. What place does aesthetic hold in your work?

Will Vogt: A very important one. I may be documenting something but I still want to make great photographs. I’ve always been conscious of composition, light and the relationship between people and the places they inhabit.

The surroundings are also part of the story. A house, a swimming pool, a shooting field or a dining room tells you something about the people in the photograph before you know anything about them. Sometimes the setting is every bit as important as the people.

In the essay he wrote to accompany These Americans , novelist Jay McInerney, author of Bright Lights, Big City , says “there’s no pane of glass” between you and your subjects. Doesn’t that closeness encroach on the distance a photographer sometimes needs from his subject?

Will Vogt: Familiarity gives me great access, but more than that it allows people to be comfortable around me and the camera. That is a tremendous advantage.

I think that is where the photographer has to create his own distance. You’re part of the scene but you’re also removed enough to document it. I’ve been doing that for most of my adult life, so I don’t think about it very consciously anymore.

One photograph in Behind the Hedges shows nothing but the filthy window of a Range Rover, finger-written with the line: “I wish my wife was as dirty as this.” The gap between a message that crude and a world that buttoned-up seems to delight you, as though you were forever hunting for the grain of sand that might jam the machine…

Will Vogt: I do like that photograph and particularly the contradiction and the humor. I don’t think I’m hunting for something to jam the machine. I’m looking for things that make the picture more complicated and thought-provoking than what you might expect.

There are plenty of preconceived ideas about this world and photographs like that one upset those expectations a little. People are rarely as buttoned-up as they appear. That’s what makes them interesting to photograph.

Behind the Hedges opens on a quote from F. Scott Fitzgerald, as an epigraph, before the first photograph. What place does literature hold in your eye as a photographer?

Will Vogt: I’ve always read a lot and I’m certainly attracted to writers who are good observers of people and social worlds. I fell in love with the writing of F. Scott Fitzgerald as a boy, about the same time I started taking pictures. He understood that wealth and privilege could be both seductive and complicated. I think I have documented some of that in my own work.

When I’m taking a photograph, I’m not thinking about Fitzgerald or trying to make an image look literary. Those connections tend to emerge later. A photograph can contain a whole story without explaining it. In that sense, I suppose photography and literature have quite a lot in common.

Behind the Hedges returns again and again to scenes of killing: a pit of zebra carcasses, partridges hung in neat rows, hares laid out on moss. What do these scenes of slaughter reveal, in your view, about this supposedly well-mannered society?

Will Vogt: I probably wouldn’t use the word slaughter. Hunting has been a large part of my life and of the world I photograph. Those images are part of the reality of it. I don’t see a reason to sanitize that reality by showing the shooting party and leaving out the dead game.

There is also a long tradition surrounding hunting, particularly in England and South Texas. The game, the land, the dogs, the people and the rituals surrounding all of it are connected. I photograph what is there and leave it to the viewer to decide what he or she thinks about it.

The English photographer Martin Parr, who died in December 2025, spent his life photographing the British middle and working classes and their mass leisure — but as an observer, from outside that world, with an eye that was affectionate and often satirical. You do the opposite: you’ve always photographed the American elite you were born into, from the inside. Do you feel any kinship with him nonetheless?

Will Vogt: Absolutely. I have always admired Martin Parr’s work. We came at our subjects from slightly different angles but I think we shared an interest in the small details that tell you something larger about people and the way they live.

Parr was brilliant at noticing things that other people walked right past. His photographs could be funny without simply making fun of people. I hope there is some of that observational quality in my work.

Jennifer Garza-Cuen, the editor of Behind the Hedges , places your work alongside Larry Sultan, Stephen Shore and Tod Papageorge. What did you take from each of them, and what shows up from those influences in your own eye?

Will Vogt: Those three photographers are masters of their craft and I am honored that anyone would mention me in the same sentence with them. Robert Frank was obviously the earliest and most important influence on my work. I have collected photographs and photography books for many years and inevitably some of what I’ve absorbed has become part of the way I see and photograph the world.

If someone opened Behind the Hedges knowing nothing about you and decided it was satire, what would you tell them?

Will Vogt: I’d tell them they are entitled to see it that way. Once you put photographs into the world, you lose control over how people interpret them.

But satire isn’t my intention. I’m not trying to celebrate these people and I’m not trying to ridicule them. I’m recording a world I know and have been part of for my entire life. There is humor in the photographs because there is humor in life. There are also contradictions and occasionally absurdity. I don’t think you have to manufacture any of that. You just have to notice it.

As a teenager, you saw Jimi Hendrix live — a world at the opposite end of the one you’ve been photographing ever since. You also cite the Beatles and Bob Dylan among your influences. Doesn’t that irreverent spirit find its extension in the way you photograph high society — as a bit of a troublemaker yourself?

Will Vogt: I like the idea of being a troublemaker, although I’m not sure I’ve earned the title.

Music was a huge influence on me when I was young and still is. Hendrix, Dylan and the Beatles all arrived at a time when a lot of accepted ideas about how you were supposed to live were being challenged. I was certainly affected by that.

Maybe some of that does show up in the photographs. I’ve never felt any obligation to make this world look the way it might like to see itself. If something is funny, strange, awkward or a little outrageous, I’m probably going to take the picture. Maybe that is my small contribution to troublemaking.

“Will Vogt: These Americans” runs through December 6, 2026 at the Art Museum of South Texas .

Behind the Hedges (2026), photographs by Will Vogt, edited and with text by Jennifer Garza-Cuen, is published by Schilt Publishing . These Americans (2023) by Will Vogt is published by Schilt Publishing .

article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Everytime

Sandra Wollner’s film, winner of Un Certain Regard at Cannes this year, is an enigmatic exploration of grief and the path to healing.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Sandra Wollner

With Birgit Minichmayr, Tristan López, Lotte Shirin Keiling

Austria-Germany 2026. 124min

Courtesy of BFI Distribution

Language German With English subtitles

Introduction

In Wollner’s lyrical and haunting third feature, a mother, a daughter and a teenage boy struggle with blame and forgiveness over a recent tragedy that saw their lives intersect. To escape their daily surroundings, they travel to Tenerife. As the long days go by under the sun and heat, reality and memories blend as each grapples with their feelings and a desire to move forward.

Isabel Moir

With thanks to the Austrian Cultural Forum London.

Content advice

Contains scenes of drug use.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra

Jacqueline Lentzou follows Moon 66 Questions with this evocative and playful look into the life of a teenager who is completely unaware of the forces at play in her fate.

Josephine

Winner of the Grand Jury Dramatic Prize at Sundance, this suspenseful and devastating film follows a child trying to navigate life after witnessing a sexual assault.

Mouse

Katherine Mallen Kupferer and Sophie Okonedo excel in this moving drama about facing up to life in the aftermath of a tragedy.

article_text:
The Republic of Austria, the Albertina Museum , and the Leopold Museum Foundation—the latter two both in Vienna—filed a response Friday to amicus briefs submitted by two US senators, in which they repeat their claim that the updated Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery (HEAR) Act violates Article III of the US Constitution and the Tenth Amendment.

Austria, the Albertina, and the Leopold are defendants in a suit brought by Timothy Reif, a descendant of Fritz Grünbaum, a Jewish cabaret performer and collector who was killed in a death camp in 1941. Reif is seeking the return of several works by Egon Schiele that he alleges were looted by the Nazis when they seized Grünbaum’s collection. The defendants dispute the claim, arguing that the works in question are part of the same cache that was exported from Austria by Grünbaum’s sister-in-law in the 1930s and then sold to a Swiss dealer in the 1950s.

Although the defendants had previously argued in several motions that the HEAR Act is unconstitutional, this new filing responds to briefs submitted last month by the Department of Justice and by Senators Richard Blumenthal (Democrat of Connecticut) and John Cornyn (Republican of Texas). Those briefs presented additional legal precedent supporting the constitutionality of the HEAR Act. Friday’s response addresses each of those cases. Though the defendants “respect the work of the Senators and the Government, and their attention to trying to remedy at least some of the horrors of the Holocaust,” they believe that in passing the amended version of HEAR, “Congress exceeded its constitutional bounds,” the filing states.

Blumenthal and Cornyn did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

At the heart of the response are the 2025 amendments to the HEAR Act, which President Donald Trump signed into law last year. Originally signed in 2016, the act was set to expire in 2026; the amendments extend it indefinitely. Other key changes were meant to address several high-profile cases that had failed in court on technical grounds, including statutes of limitations that vary depending on the state in which a case is brought.

The defendants argue that the HEAR Act stops short of creating a federal law for art restitution, akin to federal copyright law, and in doing so “delegates the substantive means to restitute Nazi-looted art to the states,” the filing reads. Courts are then to rely on applicable state laws, but by eliminating defenses based on technicalities, the 2025 changes dictate how courts should rule on the cases before them.

As a result, the defendants argue, the HEAR Act violates both the Tenth Amendment, which states that any power not explicitly granted to the federal government belongs to the states, and Article III of the Constitution, specifically the separation-of-powers doctrine, which gives courts the authority to decide the cases before them and how to rule on them.

“By forbidding the federal courts from any longer considering these equitable defenses, Congress is intruding on the constitutional right and obligation of Article III courts to ‘decide’ such cases and controversies for themselves,” the defendants’ response reads.

One defense eliminated by the 2025 amendments is laches, under which an otherwise valid claim can be dismissed if the claimant unreasonably delayed bringing it. The change bars courts from conducting “any factfinding as to questions of whether ‘inexcusable delay’ by a plaintiff or the plaintiff’s predecessors caused the loss of critical evidence, resulting in ‘unfair prejudice’ to the current owner of allegedly stolen art,” the response states.

The filing adds, “By outlawing the laches defense in particular, which prevents unprovable allegations of Nazi theft from becoming de facto conclusive presumptions of Nazi theft, the HEAR Act unquestionably does compel particular factfinding in favor of plaintiffs.”

In a phone interview, William L. Charron, an attorney for the defendants, said the purpose of Friday’s filing was to respond directly to the additional arguments for the HEAR Act’s constitutionality raised by the Justice Department and Senators Blumenthal and Cornyn.

“The government and the Senators intervened and involved themselves in this case because they wanted to be heard as to their reasons why they believe the HEAR Act is constitutional, and so this was an opportunity for my clients to respond and explain why they respectfully disagree with those positions and respectfully believe the HEAR Act is unconstitutional,” he told ARTnews .

Charron said he believes Reif v. Republic of Austria can be decided without addressing the constitutionality of the HEAR Act. But if the courts decide they must rule on that question, he said, it is the kind of case that could eventually make its way to the Supreme Court.

“I believe these are important and serious issues,” Charron said of the arguments raised in the filing. “We have given the Court a number of arguments and grounds to dismiss the case without having to rule upon these constitutional questions. But if the Court decides that it does need to address the constitutionality of the HEAR Act, I certainly hope that it seriously considers the arguments that have been raised in this filing.”

editorial_excerpt_zh: 扎克·克雷格通过摄影机选择和主角灾难性的决策，将游戏的紧张感与幽默感转化为一场让观众身临其境的冒险。文章 影评 | 《生化危机》（2026）：在没有控制权的情况下游玩 首先出现在 Cinema com Rapadura 。

"关于游戏改编电影的讨论，往往将大量注意力放在叙事忠实度上，以至于“成为一部好电影”这样最为基础的要求反而退居其次。识别出角色和彩蛋固然是乐趣的一部分，但当作品找不到一种属于自己的方式去吸引观众时，这些也无济于事。幸运的是，导演扎克·克雷格在新版《生化危机》中理解了这一优先级，并以此作为改编游戏体验的途径。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部长片聚焦于布赖恩（奥斯汀·艾布拉姆斯饰），一个对即将到来的夜晚完全没有准备的家伙。他的旅程无非是到达某个地方、弄清楚如何继续前进，并逃离路上出现的一切。这种简单性让克雷格能够将叙事集中在路线以及随之而来的困难上。看似临近的目标有时需要一连串的临场发挥和值得商榷的决策，这使得前往目的地的过程甚至比目的地等待着他的东西还要重要。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种结构为改编作品提供了自由发挥必要的基础。游戏中那些易于辨认的角色缺席了，而保护伞公司（Umbrella）和浣熊市（Raccoon City）则成了定位粉丝的短暂参考，完全不承担支撑故事的责任。导演利用这个宇宙构建了一场属于他自己的冒险，没有把大部分时长花在铺垫熟知的情节或解释每个元素如何契合时间线上面。与原作的联系是通过穿越那个世界的体验建立起来的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种选择承认了两种媒介之间根本性的差异——最终的产品被称为“改编”而不是“抄录”，是有原因的。在游戏中，前进取决于屏幕前的人，哪怕有时候内心的愿望只是停滞不前或是关掉平台以避开下一个惊吓。在电影中，旅程会无视这种意愿继续下去。克雷格试图通过在探索环境期间不断调动观众的注意力来重新创造这种沉浸感，而摄影机的选择则将这种意图付诸实现。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "取景镜头让多个点处于可疑状态，并刺激着对威胁的搜寻。总有某些部分还需要被看到，而导演将这种发现过程拉长到了足以让探索变得令人不安的程度。至于第一人称视角镜头则限制了视野，将观众的视线拉近到主角的视角。摄影机的每一次移动都会揭示一个区域并抛下另一个区域，从而加剧了危险恰恰潜伏在视线之外的紧张感。当然，你无法替布赖恩做决定，但你可以评估（并评判）他的路线、预判风险，并在他做出看似极其糟糕的决定时感到痛苦（或大笑）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管突发惊吓（jump scare）十分频繁，但它们因这种已经让观众对画面中任何变化保持警惕的氛围而受益。克雷格深知，出现某种事物的期待所带来的持续不安感，往往比事物本身出现更持久。生物以充满攻击性的动作和足够的暴力打破了这种等待，打乱了人们对其应对方式的感知。然而，这种体验也包含着荒诞，正是在各种问题的累积中，这部电影找到了它最有趣的特质。剧本构建了一种某种程度上的倒霉进程，布赖恩无法解决一个困难，紧接着就会发现另一个更糟糕的困难。正是这种让叙事不断推进的逻辑产生了喜剧效果。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不可否认，布赖恩对恶化自身处境“功不可没”。他的毫无准备远不能作为发现隐藏英雄主义的起点。他一直在搞砸事情，而电影对此心知肚明。有些决定在付诸实施之前就已经显得很糟糕了（比如那些既搞笑又烦人的挂锁桥段），而另有些决定则直到大难临头、无力回天时才暴露出灾难的程度（比如拥抱一个彻底感染的小女孩）。克雷格在对错误的预期以及对结果的反应中都找到了幽默感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，奥斯汀·艾布拉姆斯的出色表演对于平衡这一切是不可或缺的。这位演员展现出自己有能力刻画出事件的狂热节奏与布赖恩理解能力之间的脱节，就好像当下一个问题已经要求做出回应时，这个角色甚至还在试图消化之前的问题。他的惊恐以及应对一切的方式产生了一些最佳时刻，他所陷入的处境又是如此荒诞，以至于你很难不支持他完成任务——即便他表现得像个笨蛋。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有趣的是，幽默积极参与了主角的塑造以及冒险的节奏。一个反应可以在几秒钟内缓解紧张气氛，却不会让环境变得更安全，正如一个滑稽的选择随后可能会产生暴力的后果一样。这种共生关系阻止了电影落入惊吓时刻与笑料时刻之间可预测的交替套路，因为很多时候，这两种效果属于同一处境。观众一边嘲笑问题的严重性，一边仍然担心布赖恩能否摆脱困境。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本片时长1h35，在维持这一节奏的同时，无需拓展故事来证明其所改编IP的重要性。近乎实时的叙事推进极大地增强了一种感觉：这些事件并非关于那个宏大宇宙的某种宏观解释的各个阶段，而是当下必须解决的困境。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种专注也暴露出了一些局限性。到了最后一幕，这种为主角不断叠加障碍的机制已经显得十分明显，一连串的挑战最终也失去了一些冲击力。此外，试图通过加入父职关切来为布莱恩（Bryan）发展出一条戏剧性成长轨迹的空间非常有限。这一层面的处理最终显得有些可有可无，毕竟，观众与该角色的羁绊早已通过其他方式得到了确立，尤其是通过精湛的表演以及目睹其接连遭遇各种灾难的过程。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《生化危机》（Resident Evil）深知从一种媒介向另一种媒介的过渡需要重建观众的代入感。为此，克雷格（Cregger）充分利用电影工具（尤其是镜头的运用）来重现游玩生存恐怖游戏时的感受。成片既紧张又趣味十足，成功保留了穿越敌意之地的痛苦与那种难以言喻的快感，哪怕观众对整个行程没有任何掌控权。布莱恩则负责让这段旅程尽可能地变得一团糟。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Zach Cregger traduz a tensão e o humor dos jogos em uma aventura que envolve o espectador pelas escolhas de câmera e pelas decisões desastrosas de seu protagonista.

A discussão sobre adaptações de jogos para o cinema costuma dedicar tanta atenção à fidelidade narrativa que uma exigência tão básica quanto “ser um bom filme” pode ficar em segundo plano. Reconhecer personagens e referências faz parte do prazer, mas pouco adianta quando a obra não encontra uma maneira própria de envolver o público. Felizmente, o diretor Zach Cregger compreende essa prioridade no novo “ Resident Evil ” e faz dela o caminho para adaptar a experiência dos games.

O longa acompanha Bryan (Austin Abrams), um sujeito completamente despreparado para a noite que terá pela frente. Sua jornada se resume a chegar a um lugar, descobrir como prosseguir e escapar do que aparecer pelo caminho. Essa simplicidade permite que Cregger concentre a narrativa no percurso e nas dificuldades que se apresentam. Objetivos aparentemente próximos por vezes exigem uma sequência de improvisos e decisões questionáveis que tornam o deslocamento até mais importante do que o que o espera no destino.

Essa estrutura oferece a base necessária para a adaptação trabalhar com liberdade. Os personagens reconhecíveis dos jogos estão ausentes, enquanto Umbrella e Raccoon City servem como breves referências para localizar os fãs, sem assumir qualquer responsabilidade de sustentar a história. O diretor utiliza o universo para construir uma aventura própria, sem gastar boa parte da duração preparando acontecimentos conhecidos ou explicando como cada elemento se encaixa na cronologia. O vínculo com o material original se estabelece pela experiência de atravessar aquele mundo.

Essa escolha reconhece uma diferença fundamental entre as duas mídias — há uma razão para o produto final se chamar “adaptação”, não “transcrição”. No jogo, avançar depende de quem está diante da tela, inclusive quando a vontade é apenas permanecer parado ou desligar a plataforma para evitar o próximo susto. No cinema, o percurso continua independentemente dessa disposição. Cregger busca recriar esse envolvimento exercitando constantemente a atenção do público durante a exploração dos ambientes, e as escolhas de câmera concretizam essa intenção.

Os enquadramentos mantêm vários pontos sob suspeita e estimulam a busca por ameaças. Há sempre alguma parte que ainda precisa ser vista, e a direção prolonga essa descoberta o suficiente para tornar a exploração desconfortável. Já as cenas em primeira pessoa restringem a visão, aproximando o olhar do espectador da perspectiva do protagonista. Cada movimento de câmera revela uma área e abandona outra, alimentando a tensão de que o perigo esteja justamente onde não dá para ver. Não é possível decidir por Bryan, claro, mas é possível avaliar (e julgar) seus caminhos, antecipar os riscos e sofrer (ou rir) quando ele faz exatamente o que parecia ser uma péssima ideia.

Embora sejam frequentes, os sustos repentinos se beneficiam dessa atmosfera que já deixou o público atento a qualquer mudança no quadro. Cregger sabe que a expectativa de uma aparição pode sustentar o desconforto por mais tempo do que a aparição em si. As criaturas rompem a espera com movimentos agressivos e violência suficientes para desestabilizar a percepção de como enfrentá-las. Mas essa experiência também comporta o absurdo, e é no acúmulo de problemas que o filme encontra sua característica mais divertida. O roteiro constrói uma espécie de progressão da desgraça na qual Bryan é incapaz de concluir uma dificuldade sem descobrir outra ainda pior. A mesma lógica que mantém a narrativa em movimento produz comédia.

É inegável o quanto Bryan contribui para piorar as próprias circunstâncias. Sua falta de preparo está longe de servir como ponto de partida para a descoberta de um heroísmo escondido. Ele faz besteira o tempo todo, e o filme tem plena consciência disso. Algumas decisões já parecem ruins antes mesmo de serem colocadas em prática (como as hilárias e irritantes sequências com os cadeados), enquanto outras só revelam a extensão do desastre quando já não há muito a fazer (como abraçar uma garotinha para lá de infectada). Cregger encontra humor tanto na antecipação do erro quanto na reação ao resultado.

Dessa forma, o bom trabalho de Austin Abrams é indispensável para equilibrar tudo. O ator se mostra capaz de retratar esse descompasso entre o ritmo frenético dos acontecimentos e a capacidade de Bryan compreendê-los, como se o personagem ainda estivesse tentando processar o problema anterior quando o seguinte já exige uma resposta. Seu espanto e a maneira de lidar com tudo rendem alguns dos melhores momentos, e a situação em que ele se coloca é tão absurda que é difícil não torcer para ele concluir sua missão — mesmo quando se comporta como um idiota.

É interessante observar que o humor participa ativamente da construção do protagonista e do ritmo da aventura. Uma reação pode aliviar a tensão por alguns segundos sem tornar o ambiente mais seguro, assim como uma escolha engraçada pode produzir consequências violentas logo depois. Essa simbiose impede que o filme se acomode num revezamento previsível entre a hora do susto e a hora da piada porque, muitas vezes, os dois efeitos pertencem à mesma situação. O espectador ri do tamanho do problema enquanto continua preocupado com a possibilidade de Bryan não conseguir sair dele.

Com 1h35 de duração, o longa mantém essa dinâmica sem precisar expandir a história para justificar a importância da propriedade intelectual que está adaptando. A progressão quase em tempo real favorece bastante a sensação de que os acontecimentos não são etapas de uma explicação maior sobre aquele universo, e sim dificuldades que precisam ser resolvidas agora.

Essa concentração também expõe algumas limitações. No ato final, esse mecanismo de acumular obstáculos para o protagonista já está bem evidente, e a sucessão de desafios acaba perdendo parte do impacto. Além disso, a tentativa de desenvolver uma trajetória dramática para Bryan acrescentando uma preocupação com a paternidade recebe bem pouco espaço para amadurecer. Essa camada acaba parecendo dispensável, afinal, o vínculo com o personagem já era convincente por outros meios, sobretudo pela atuação e pela convivência com sua sucessão de calamidades.

“Resident Evil” reconhece que a passagem de uma mídia para outra exige reconstruir o envolvimento do público. Para isso, Cregger aposta nas ferramentas do cinema (principalmente o uso da câmera) para recriar o sentimento de jogar um terror de sobrevivência. O resultado é tenso e muito divertido, sendo capaz de preservar a aflição e o prazer inexplicável de atravessar um lugar hostil, mesmo sem oferecer qualquer controle sobre o percurso. Bryan se encarrega de tornar essa jornada o mais desastrosa possível.

title_original: Als het verleden begint te muteren – over het werk van Natasha Tontey bij 1646
editorial_title_zh: 当过去开始突变——娜塔莎·通蒂在1646的作品
editorial_excerpt_zh: 历史并非凝固不变，而是一个可以不断被赋予新形态的给定事实。米纳哈萨艺术家娜塔莎·通蒂（Natasha Tontey）的思辨性电影装置正是如此。在海牙1646举办的她的个展《Macho Mystic Meltdown: Substracted Anthology》中……

article_text:
Geschiedenis is niet gestold, maar is een gegeven dat constant opnieuw gestalte kan krijgen. Dat is wat de Minahassische kunstenaar Natasha Tontey met haar speculatieve filminstallaties doet. In haar solotentoonstelling Macho Mystic Meltdown: Substracted Anthology bij 1646 in Den Haag worden de poreuze grenzen tussen herkenbaarheid en fictie opgezocht. ‘Natasha’s werk lijkt gebeurtenissen op het snijvlak van herinnering en mythe te reconstrueren, telkens nieuwe configuraties uitproberend. Zoals een helder droombeeld dat je wilt beschrijven, maar oplost zodra je inzoomt op de details. Humor kan zo plots sarcastisch worden, en lieflijke gebaren kunnen vervormen tot monsterlijke woede.’ Paoletta Holst bezocht de tentoonstelling en ging dieper in op deze droombeelden.

Zoom in: kauwen met voedsel tussen de tanden, en lachen, manisch lachen, hysterisch lachen. Zoom uit: Een eitje bakken op een blauw vuurtje. Reizen op een dolfijn door een nachtelijke oceaan. Stapels eierdozen in de hoek van de ruimte. Militair ritmisch stampvoeten. Een fragiel ouder wordend lichaam dat zichzelf toont in mannelijkheid én onzekerheid. Een eiershake maken, voor wat extra proteïne. De ruimte: donker, met een accent van diepblauw blacklight dat contrasteert met de overwegend oranjeachtige filmprojectie en tafeltjes met geruite kleedjes waarachter je kunt plaatsnemen.

Het zijn enkele willekeurige, in elkaar hakende beelden en ervaringen uit Natasha Tontey’s drie immersieve filminstallaties in haar solotentoonstelling Macho Mystic Meltdown: Substracted Anthology bij 1646 in Den Haag. Wat aantrekt in haar installaties is precies de speelsheid waarmee poreuze grenzen tussen herkenbaarheid en fictie worden opgezocht. Met name de momenten waarop personen hun eigen persiflage worden. Zoals in Chapter 4: In a Muscle Mood , waarin Beetje, een Minahasa Permesta-oorlogsveteraan, zijn verouderde, gespierde en door oorlog getekende lichaam toont. Zijn lichaam draagt niet alleen het gewicht van een geschiedenis, maar vormt ook het vertrekpunt voor Natasha om thema’s als trauma, zorg en kwetsbare mannelijkheid in postkoloniaal Indonesië te verkennen. Lichamen dragen geweld en intimiteit met zich mee, in overgeërfde herinneringen, gebaren, spanningen en trauma’s.

Natasha’s werk lijkt gebeurtenissen op het snijvlak van herinnering en mythe te reconstrueren, telkens nieuwe configuraties uitproberend. Zoals een helder droombeeld dat je wilt beschrijven, maar oplost zodra je inzoomt op de details. Humor kan zo plots sarcastisch worden, en lieflijke gebaren kunnen vervormen tot monsterlijke woede. In Natasha’s eigen woorden: ‘Voor mij is het verleden niet iets nostalgisch of vaststaands. Het gedraagt zich eerder als voorlevend materiaal: het muteert, spookt, vermomt zich en keert soms terug als een monster, een grap of een vervormd beeld.’ [1]

Collectieve geschiedenissen kunnen zich zo vermengen met persoonlijke verhalen, en persoonlijke herinneringen met collectieve. Dit roept de bredere vraag op naar wat er achterblijft. Hoe onthouden we wat we zien en ervaren? Hoe geven we het een plaats en laten we het voortbestaan? Eén antwoord zou kunnen zijn, het zogenaamd objectief documenteren, categoriseren, annoteren en bewaren van gebeurtenissen, bijvoorbeeld in archieven voor toekomstige generaties. Dat is een dominante manier waarop geschiedenis hier, in Nederland en op veel andere plekken, wordt vastgelegd: als iets dat zich in het verleden afspeelt en voortleeft in bevroren beelden en documenten. Voor subjectieve interpretatie, fictie en speculatie lijkt daarbinnen weinig ruimte, waardoor vele verhalen en ervaringen onderbelicht blijven of vermeden worden.

Dit komt naar voren in Chapter 2: Monster; She Wrote . Daarin herinterpreteert Natasha het verhaal van een beruchte Minahasa-strijdster uit de jaren vijftig, die tijdens de Permesta-oorlog in Indonesië beviel terwijl ze ondergedoken zat. Ze weet zowel het militarisme van de strijdster als haar veronderstelde biologische bestemming ter discussie te stellen.

De vraag die Natasha bezighoudt is welke toekomst en wiens toekomst het verleden mogelijk maakt: ‘De toekomst wordt voor mij gevormd door wat is onderdrukt, verkeerd herinnerd of onafgemaakt is gebleven. Ze groeit voort uit onopgeloste geschiedenissen, voorouderlijke overleveringen, beschadigde archieven en vormen van kennis die vaak als irrationeel, marginaal of achterhaald worden beschouwd.’ Haar filminstallaties brengen dit indringend en humorvol naar voren. Geschiedenissen en herinneringen zijn geen passieve, maar actieve verbeeldingsoefeningen die het mogelijk maken ons een andere toekomst voor te stellen.

article_text:
Photobook design workshop with Ann Griffin took place from March 7-10, 2024 organized by Matca and supported by the Swiss Arts Council Pro Helvetia. During the intensive 4-day course, participants went through the process of making a photobook, from brainstorming concepts, photo editing, and designing the layout, to considering physical attributes of the publication like materials and printing techniques. They also discussed at length issues in producing and distributing photobooks in the context of Switzerland and Vietnam.

Despite the time limitation, instructor Ann Griffin and 9 participants including photographers and graphic designers have created a friendly and constructive learning space. Let’s take a look at some excerpts from their final works.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Xanh Loanh Quanh (Green All Around) – Phan Hồng Khang

Daily items of various shades of green/blue appear in familiar and unexpected spots in Saigon.

Size: 22×30 cm; number of pages: 50

Dinner for Ten – Linh DN

Observations in the kitchen – a gathering space of a big family including three cats and one dog.

Size: 9,8×14,5 cm; number of pages: 68

Nội – Tùng Xuân Lâm

An exploration of shifting colors, lines and shapes on the street of Hanoi.

Size: 16 x 23,5 cm; number of pages: 40

Mưa (When It Rains) – Nguyễn Ngọc Hải

Tragicomic moments when stuck in traffic in the heavy rain made lively with a direct flash.

Size: 22×29,5 cm; number of pages: 84

First Look – Hùng Ngọ

The familiar and funny on the street of Hanoi as captured by a young photographer.

Size: 14,5×21 cm; number of pages: 44

Crimson Heart – Hoàng Nguyễn

Combining self-portraits and still life, the photographer tells the ups and downs of a relationship with a red chrysanthemum.

Size: 14,5×19,5 cm; number of pages: 60

The Quick Brown Fox Jumps Over The Lazy Dog – Ngô Lan Phương

Inspired by literacy books for children, the alphabet is retold through abstract and mundane objects.

Size: 14,5×21 cm; number of pages: 72

Untitled – Charlie Moore

Quiet moments captured by a British photographer during five years living in Vietnam.

Size: 14,5 x 21 cm; number of pages: 60

31 – Phương Hoàng

Struck by the death of 39 Vietnamese nationals in a container, Phuong Hoang visits and documents a village in Nghe An where unfortunate victims came from.

Size: 10,5×29,5 cm; number of pages: 44

article_text:
Tree Week: Han Sungpil: Frozen Fire

©Han Sungpil, North Saskathewan River, Crossing, Banff National Park, from Frozen Fire series

The first time I saw Han Sungpil ’s work, there was a small crowd leaning over the images in reverential silence. I looked at the photos from the back of the crowd, and saw a multitude of black lines on pristine white paper. When I was able to get closer, I saw that each of the lines was a blackened tree lying on a bed of snow. Sungpil explained that this portfolio, “ Frozen Fire ,” was taken in the Canadian Rockies in the aftermath of the wildfires. The devastation was horrific, yet seen through Sungpil’s lens, the patterns looked like delicate brushstrokes. The contrast of the ruin with the artistry of Sungpil’s compositions is striking, and makes these images have lasting impact.

Han Sungpil’s work is inspired by the fragile balance between loss and renewal. His love of the Rocky Mountains is one thing that drew Han to immigrate to Canada from his native Korea. He brings an understanding of traditional Korean landscape painting to his current work, “Frozen Fire.” The Eastern philosophy of impermanence is combined with his direct encounters with the aftermath of the Canadian wildfires. He said, “Standing amid the charred remains, I often felt as though the once-mighty forest had never existed. Silence and stillness prevailed, broken only by the slow, patient work of natural regeneration.”

©Han Sungpil, Waterton Lakes National Park, from Frozen Fire series

Han Sungpil is a multidisciplinary visual artist born in Korea and based in Calgary, Canada. Moving across photography, video and installation, his work begins with a single fundamental question: how have the accumulated actions of humanity, across centuries, quietly reshaped the world we inhabit today? His practice explores the intersection of nature, human impact and environmental change, and the awe inspiring majesty of the natural world remains a driving force in both his life and his art.

Instagram: @han_sugpgil

©Han Sungpil, Waterton Lakes National Park, from Frozen Fire series

What drew you to photograph the aftermath of the Canadian fires, and how did you feel when you saw all the damage.

It was March 2020 when I moved to Canada. However, the day after my arrival, the Canadian border was closed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In a strange land where I knew no one, my activities ground to a halt for over three years, and I had to sustain life merely for survival. This period was a painful time of isolation and vacancy. However, in May 2021, I accidentally encountered massive ecological scars at Waterton Lakes National Park. The Kenow wildfire, which originated in British Columbia in 2017, turned about 40 percent of Waterton Lakes National Park in Alberta to ash and spread across the border to reduce Glacier National Park in Montana, USA, to ash as well. That dystopian landscape felt like a mirror reflecting my lost inner self. However, a sudden heavy snowfall the following morning completely transformed the scenery. Before the landscape where pure white snow settled over black, charred trees, I reencountered the Eastern philosophical notions of emptiness (yeobaek) and impermanence. It was the emptiness of traditional Korean painting and the impermanence of Eastern philosophy. Emptiness is not a vacant space, but a generative void left empty so that new possibilities may emerge; impermanence is not futility, but a cyclical philosophy holding that nothing is fixed forever and destruction is merely a phase of rebirth. The snow-covered land was a void emptied for new life to emerge, which would melt into water in spring to become nourishment for new life, and the sprouts budding beneath the charred trunks demonstrated that destruction is not the end.

©Han Sungpil, Waterton Lakes National Park, from Frozen Fire series

You had mentioned to me that the temperature got to -30 Celsius, and I’d like to know what it was like to work under such extreme temperatures. Did you have issues with your equipment?

In the Canadian Rockies, the temperature sometimes drops below -30 degrees Celsius. However, because I kept walking and hiking for shooting, my body generated heat, so it didn’t feel that cold. I only felt the cold during the 30-odd minutes spent setting up the tripod and shooting. There were no major issues with shooting because I wrapped the camera warmly and kept it well-stored in the camera bag away from the cold air. Additionally, I prepared for emergencies by keeping spare batteries and memory cards warm in my jacket using hand warmers.

©Han Sungpil, Grisette Mountain and Mount Dromore, Jasper National Park, from Frozen Fire series

©Han Sungpil, North Saskatchewan River, Crossing, Banff National Park, from Frozen Fire series

How long could you stay outside before needing to warm up?

For shooting, I sometimes stayed in the mountains for 2 days and 1 night, or 3 days and 2 nights. Deep in the Canadian Rockies, there are huts or lodges operated for backcountry skiers and winter mountaineers. Once a shooting schedule was set, I planned a hiking route on the map, booked a remote hut or lodge in advance, hiked for 7 to 9 hours to reach it, and worked while staying there.

©Han Sungpil, Chetamon Mountain, Jasper National Park, from Frozen Fire series

When holding one of your prints, I was struck by tactile nature of the paper, and how that added to the viewing experience. Can you tell us the name of the paper and why you chose it?

I printed this work on Hanji, a traditional Korean paper. Hanji is made through a long process: stripping the bark of paper mulberry, boiling it, beating it, mixing it in water, and scooping it out layer by layer. No step can be rushed. Hanji is the embodiment of an ancient philosophy of patience and devotion, a way of life that reaches completion precisely by not rushing. As the old saying goes, “Paper lasts a thousand years, while silk lasts five hundred years” (紙千年 絹五百), paper made this way withstands the test of time. The decades it takes for a burnt forest to become a forest once again is also time that cannot be rushed.

Hanji is a paper born from trees. I place the image of a burnt tree back onto paper derived from a tree. The memory of the destroyed forest seeps into the fibers of another tree. The intertwined fibers of Hanji resemble the roots and new sprouts reaching out again from under the ashes.
